identification.title: Wonderful Merciful Savior
identification.notes: Written by Dawn Rodgers and Eric Wyse in 1989; copyright Word Music / Dayspring Music, with Curb Word Music and Warner Chappell named on other pages; CCLI 106879 per hymnary's record. The list's writer credit is right; some sources spell the surname Rogers. Rodgers began it during her own devotions while Wyse was travelling, and they finished the verses together after he returned. Her stated plan was a Trinitarian hymn, with sections turning to the Son, the Spirit and the Father. Selah's recording is the version most churches know, though the song predates it. No album was verified from a fetched source. Reviewed as the song, not as any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: Three short verses, one for each Person of the Trinity (Son, Spirit, Father), each followed by the same refrain, which is sung once more at the end. The first verse addresses Christ as Savior, Redeemer and friend and marvels that a sacrificial lamb rescues souls. The second addresses the Spirit as counselor, comforter and keeper who gives hope to the lost. The third addresses the Father as faithful, almighty and loving, who meets us in weakness as we come before his throne. The refrain praises and adores the one who gives the healing and grace hearts hunger for. The cross and resurrection are not named.

claims.claim: Christ is Savior, Redeemer and friend, the Lamb whose sacrifice rescues human souls.
claims.subject: Christ the Savior

claims.claim: The Holy Spirit is counselor, comforter and keeper, giving hope to the lost.
claims.subject: The Holy Spirit

claims.claim: The Father is faithful, almighty and loving toward his own, and meets us in weakness as we come before his throne.
claims.subject: God the Father

claims.claim: The church praises and adores the one who gives the healing and grace hearts hunger for.
claims.subject: Grace and worship

claims.claim: Each Person of the Trinity is addressed in turn, so the whole is praise of the triune God.
claims.subject: The Trinity

strengths.title: Praise offered to all three Persons
strengths.explanation: Each verse turns to one Person: Son, Spirit and Father. A congregation sings to the triune God and learns the Spirit's comfort and keeping and the Father's faithfulness alongside the Son's rescue.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Grace of the Lord Jesus, love of God, fellowship of the Spirit - the three Persons the hymn addresses.

strengths.title: Christ's titles gathered as worship
strengths.explanation: The first verse names Christ as Savior, Redeemer and friend and the Lamb whose sacrifice rescues souls. It says what he has done for sinners, not only how the singer feels.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world - the figure the refrain uses.

strengths.title: Weakness brought to the Father's throne
strengths.explanation: The third verse says the Father meets us in our weakness as we come before his throne, which gives the singer confidence to draw near.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Approaching the throne of grace to find help in time of need.

doctrinesAffirmed: Christ as the Lamb who rescues sinners
The Spirit as counselor and comforter
Access to God's throne in weakness
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct was found. The song addresses the Son, the Spirit and the Father in turn and presents mercy and grace as God's gift. The gospel is carried by the Lamb imagery; the cross and resurrection are not named, which is a thin spot rather than an error.

strengths.title: A gentle, memorable melody
strengths.explanation: One church's hymnbook entry describes the melody as gentle and distinct from the exuberant praise songs of its era, which suits a congregation singing together rather than following a leader.

communal.vocalRangeNote: Published keys were not checked; choose one in rehearsal that keeps the refrain comfortable for untrained voices.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The same refrain follows each verse and is sung again at the end, with a short echo line closing each section. The repetition is heavy but keeps the song on praise of God's grace.
communal.assessment: Congregational in form: short lines, simple structure and a refrain sung three times and once more, so it is easy to learn. Its Trinitarian shape suits Communion, times of confession and gatherings wanting a quieter response to the gospel.

strengths.title: The Persons are named
strengths.explanation: Each verse opens by naming the Person addressed (Son, Spirit, Father), so the addressee is always clear.

clarity.assessment: Clear. The titles are biblical and each verse is plainly addressed. It states less of the gospel's sequence than a narrative hymn would, which limits how much a visitor learns but does not confuse.

synthesis.summary: A 1989 hymn by Dawn Rodgers and Eric Wyse praising the Trinity, with a verse each for Son, Spirit and Father and a shared refrain asking for healing and grace. No theological concern was found; the gospel content is thin, with the Lamb imagery but no named cross or resurrection.

scriptureReferences.relevance: The Lamb of God who takes away sin - the figure in the refrain.
The Spirit given as helper and comforter - the second section's subject.
The three Persons named together - the hymn's Trinitarian frame.
Coming to the throne to find grace - the third verse.
